newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds says smokers spurned low tar cigarettes.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds says smokers spurned low tar cigarettes.

text.p: The chief of development at R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. told a court hearing a wrongful death suit Thursday that smokers had spurned cigarettes with a lower tar and nicotine content.

David Townsend, the first defence witness and director of product development and assessment for Reynolds, said the company had made "extraordinary efforts" to reduce tar, nicotine and other elements deemed harmful to health by medical experts.
It had introduced filters, extracted elements and tried different ways of ventilating cigarettes.
Consumers rejected the cigarettes as they did not taste good, he said.

Over 1992 and 1993, Reynolds developed a cigarette called Premier in what he called the most intense project it had ever undertaken. When it was test-marketed , it was a resounding failure, Townsend said.
The company was currently test-marketing in Tennessee another product called Eclipse which he called the "most advanced cigarette design" he had seen.
In the case, plaintiff Dana Raulerson is suing Reynolds on behalf of the estate and children of Jean Connor, her sister, who died of lung cancer at age 49.
Earlier Thursday, Circuit Judge Bernard Nachman dismissed one juror from the panel, leaving no alternates.

The juror, Sandra Grant, told Reuters as she rushed from the courthouse that her mother-in-law was dying. She said she had asked Nachman if she could be off on Friday and Monday but he did not want to hold up the trial and excused her.
R.J. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
